svg.title: Theoretical ATT&CK mapping versus empirical measured coverage
svg.desc: Two panels compared. Theoretical mapping is sourced from vendor documentation and static rule tags and is blind to pipeline outages, broken parsers, EDR exclusions, and un-tuned filters. Empirical coverage is sourced from executed atomic tests and verified alerts; it closes those gaps but remains blind to agent-only execution paths, benign-payload telemetry divergence, and test-versus-production drift.
svg.text: Theoretical mapping vs. empirical measured coverage
THEORETICAL MAPPING
Asserted from documentation
• Source: vendor documentation & static rule tags
• Establishes only that a rule is claimed to exist
• Blind to: ingestion outages, broken parsers,
EDR exclusions, un-tuned suppression filters
• Refreshed by: static documentation review
EMPIRICAL MEASURED COVERAGE
Demonstrated by execution
• Source: executed atomic tests & verified alerts
• Establishes that the alert actually fired, when
• Still blind to: agent-only execution paths,
benign-payload divergence, test-vs-prod drift
• Refreshed by: scheduled CI/CD execution runs
testing
closes
the gap
Execution reduces unverified assumptions — it does not eliminate them.
A passing atomic proves that one payload, on one host build, produced one alert on the day it ran.
